title: runner watch ends a live worker whose report file is still empty, since dispatch creates result.json empty at the start
goal: backlog.py runner watch counts a report file only once it holds output: an empty file is the same as one not written yet, so a live worker is never ended for an old empty result.json (dispatch and its launcher create SCRATCH/result.json empty at the start, and claude -p --output-format json writes it when the session ends), while a written report older than --stale with the process still running is ended as today

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading, time
def run(report_text):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        c = os.path.join(d, "claude")
        open(c, "w").write("#!/bin/sh\nsleep 4\n")
        os.chmod(c, 0o755)
        rep = os.path.join(d, "result.json")
        open(rep, "w").write(report_text)
        old = time.time() - 3600
        os.utime(rep, (old, old))
        p = subprocess.Popen([c])
        threading.Thread(target=p.wait, daemon=True).start()
        time.sleep(0.5)
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "runner", "watch", "--pid", str(p.pid), "--report", rep, "--stale", "2"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
        if p.poll() is None:
            p.kill()
        assert r.returncode == 0, ("runner watch exit", r.returncode, r.stderr[-200:])
        return r.stdout + r.stderr
empty = run("")
assert "sent SIGTERM" not in empty, "runner watch ended a live worker whose report file is still empty"
full = run("{}")
assert "sent SIGTERM" in full, "runner watch no longer ends a runner that stays after a written report"

notes: Retro finding of the drain: runner watch armed right after dispatch with --report result.json --stale 600 ended a live worker (exit 143). Premise (reproduces: the repro): cmd_runner_watch (bl_procs.py) reads the report's age from st_mtime and takes only a missing file as not written yet, but bl_dispatch.run_direct opens SCRATCH/result.json for writing at the start and run_launched's shell line redirects into it, and claude -p --output-format json writes its JSON only when the session ends, so an empty file with the dispatch's start time exists from the first second and the watch ends the worker as soon as the session outlasts --stale. The fix is in runner watch, not dispatch, because the launcher's redirect creates the file in a shell dispatch does not control; kb/_self/tools.md already says a report not yet written never ends the watch, so an empty one is that case. The repro plants a fake claude and an empty and a written report with an old mtime; its second case keeps the stay-after-report watchdog working.
